claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has a single-phase BCC structure.
Untreated equal-atomic NbMoTaW has excellent high-temperature mechanical properties.
Untreated equal-atomic NbMoTaW has poor room-temperature ductility.
Irradiation resistance has been predicted for untreated equal-atomic NbMoTaW.
Controlled cold rolling followed by rapid annealing will refine the grain structure of equal-atomic NbMoTaW.
Controlled cold rolling followed by rapid annealing will produce a high density of deformation twins and/or low-angle grain boundaries.
The thermomechanical treatment will activate additional room-temperature deformation by twinning.
The thermomechanical treatment will activate additional room-temperature deformation by grain-boundary sliding.
The thermomechanical treatment will preserve the alloy's single-phase BCC structure.
The additional deformation mechanisms will increase room-temperature ductility relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Treated NbMoTaW will maintain the untreated alloy's high-temperature strength at 1600 °C.
Treated NbMoTaW will maintain the untreated alloy's irradiation-resistance characteristics.
Preservation of the single-phase BCC structure and microstructural stability will prevent degradation of high-temperature performance.
Preservation of the single-phase BCC structure and microstructural stability will prevent degradation of irradiation resistance.
Cold-rolling strain and rapid-annealing parameters must be controlled to avoid phase decomposition or other undesirable microstructural changes.
Suboptimal thermomechanical processing may degrade high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance.
